in_arabic.name: خطيب
in_arabic.meaning: من يخطب في الناس، المتكلم، خطيب الجمعة
in_arabic.long_meaning: الخطيب هو الشخص الذي يخطب في الناس، ويتكلم أمامهم، وخاصة في منصب خطيب الجمعة في الإسلام. يأتي الاسم من الجذر اللغوي 'خَطَبَ' الذي يعني التحدث أو النطق. في القرآن الكريم، لا يوجد ذكر مباشر للاسم 'خطيب'، ولكن في الحديث النبوي والتراث الإسلامي، يُستخدم مصطلح 'خطيب' للإشارة إلى الشخص الذي يلقي الخطب والمواعظ الدينية. يعتبر اسم خطيب ذا أهمية كبيرة في التراث الإسلامي، حيث يرتبط بالدعوة إلى الله تعالى ونشر العلم والوعظ.

in_urdu.name: خطیب
in_urdu.meaning: وہ شخص جو لوگوں کے سامنے خطبہ دیتا ہے، خطیب جمعہ
in_urdu.long_meaning: خطیب وہ شخص ہوتا ہے جو لوگوں کے سامنے خطبہ دیتا ہے، خاص طور پر جمعہ کے دن خطیب جمعہ. یہ نام عربی جڑ 'خَطَبَ' سے ماخوذ ہے جس کا مطلب ہے بولنا یاพูดنا. اگرچہ قرآن کریم میں 'خطیب' کا براہ راست ذکر نہیں ہے، لیکن حدیث نبوی اور اسلامی روایت میں 'خطیب' کی اصطلاح اس شخص کے لئے استعمال ہوتی ہے جو خطب اور مذہبی وعظ پیش کرتا ہے. اسلامی روایت میں خطیب کا نام بہت اہمیت کا حامل ہے، کیونکہ یہ اللہ تعالی کی دعوت اور علم اور وعظ کے پھیلاؤ سے منسلک ہے.

in_hindi.name: ख़तीब
in_hindi.meaning: वह व्यक्ति जो लोगों के सामने भाषण देता है, जुमे का ख़तीब
in_hindi.long_meaning: ख़तीब वह व्यक्ति होता है जो लोगों के सामने भाषण देता है, विशेष रूप से जुमे के दिन जुमे का ख़तीब. यह नाम अरबी मूल 'خَطَبَ' से लिया गया है जिसका अर्थ है बोलना या कहना. हालाँकि कुरआन में 'ख़तीब' का सीधा उल्लेख नहीं है, लेकिन हदीसों और इस्लामी परंपरा में 'ख़तीब' शब्द का उपयोग उस व्यक्ति के लिए किया जाता है जो धार्मिक प्रवचन और उपदेश प्रस्तुत करता है. इस्लामी परंपरा में ख़तीब नाम का बहुत महत्व है, क्योंकि यह अल्लाह की ओर बुलाने और ज्ञान तथा उपदेश के प्रसार से जुड़ा है.

in_pashto.name: خطیب
in_pashto.meaning: هغه څوک چې د خلکو په وړاندې خطبه کوي، د جمعې خطیب
in_pashto.long_meaning: خطیب هغه څوک دی چې د خلکو په وړاندې خطبه کوي، په ځانګړي ډول د جمعې په ورځ د جمعې خطیب. دا نوم د عربي ريښې 'خَطَبَ' څخه اخيستل شوی دی چې معنی يې ده وينا يا خبري اتي. که څه هم په قرآن کريم کې د 'خطیب' مستقيم ذکر نه دی، مګر په نبوي حدیث او اسلامي دود کې د 'خطیب' اصطلاح د هغه چا لپاره کارول کیږي چې دیني خطبې او وعظ وړاندې کوي. په اسلامي دود کې خطیب نوم ډیر اهمیت لري، ځکه چې دا د الله تعالی دعوت او د پوهې او وعظ د خپرولو سره تړاو لري.

in_english.name: Khathib
in_english.meaning: One who delivers a sermon or speech, especially on Fridays
in_english.long_meaning: Khathib is a name that refers to a person who delivers sermons or speeches, particularly on Fridays in an Islamic context. The term originates from the Arabic root 'خَطَبَ' (khaṭaba), meaning 'to speak' or 'to address'. Although not directly mentioned in the Quran, the term 'Khathib' is used in Prophetic traditions and Islamic heritage to describe a person who gives religious discourses and sermons. The name holds significant importance in Islamic tradition as it relates to calling to God and spreading knowledge and religious guidance. Historically, a Khathib was a respected figure responsible for leading congregational prayers and delivering sermons on Fridays, playing a vital role in religious and community life.

data.cultural_impact: The name 'Khathib' is often associated with the roles of scholars, preachers, and orators in Islamic culture. Those bearing this name have been profoundly influential in shaping the intellectual and spiritual landscape of Muslim communities throughout history. Khathibs have traditionally been respected figures, known for their mastery of language, wisdom, and ability to inspire and guide their followers. Their passionate and eloquent speeches have united and uplifted communities during times of hardship and strife, and their teachings have provided valuable guidance on the path to living a virtuous and fulfilling life.
data.spiritual_significance: The name 'Khathib' holds deep spiritual significance as it reflects the importance of effective communication and encouragement in the Islamic tradition. Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is reported to have said, "The Messenger of Allah (Peace be upon him) said, 'Verily, there is behind every one of you a crowd that will enter paradise and a crowd that will enter the fire, and encourage one another with the good.''' (Tirmidhi). The Khathib serves as a living embodiment of this hadith, working tirelessly to spread the message of Allah (SWT) and inspire those around them to strive for their spiritual growth. Their words are a reminder that language has the power to transform lives, and that each of us has a role to play in bringing about positive change in our communities and in the world at large.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Abi Shaybah in his 'Al-Musannaf' mentions a narration about a man named Khathib al-Ansari who narrated hadith from Ibn Umar. This indicates that Khathib was a prominent figure in the early Islamic period, likely in the 8th century.

historical_references.reference: Al-Dhahabi in his 'Tadhkirat al-Huffaz' mentions that Khathib al-Ansari was a prominent scholar and teacher in the early Islamic period, and that he was a student of Imam Malik. He was also known for his extensive knowledge of the Quran and Sunnah.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Khathib' originated from the Arabic word 'Khutbah' which means 'a sermon' or 'speech'. A 'Khathib' is a person who delivers the khutbah or the Friday sermon in a mosque. In modern times, the role of a Khathib has expanded beyond the physical mosque setting. They are now seen delivering sermons through various digital platforms including social media and educational institutions. This trend is driven by the increasing importance of religious education and community outreach in the digital age. Khathibs use social media platforms such as YouTube, Facebook, and Twitter to reach wider audiences and engage with their followers in real-time. Educational institutions, including universities and madrasas, also employ Khathibs to deliver sermons and religious education to their students. The role of a Khathib has become increasingly important in promoting religious literacy and fostering a sense of community among Muslims in the digital age.
